parts: What's an average charcuterie board price per size?

It depends quite a bit on size, ingredients, and whether you’re buying pre-made or DIY’ing it — but here’s a rough breakdown of what “average” charcuterie-board prices look like, by size. ## 🎯 Typical Price Ranges by Size / Guests | Size / Serving Size | Typical Price Range | |---------------------|--------------------| | Small (≈ 1–3 people / snack-size) | **~ \$20 – \$60** citeturn0search24turn0search0turn0search16 | | Medium (≈ 4–6 people, small gathering) | **~ \$50 – \$120** (for DIY-style) citeturn0search24turn0search19
Commercial/ catering medium boards often run **\$75 – \$145** depending on scope and ingredients. citeturn0search0turn0search6 | | Large (≈ 8–12 people / party-sized) | **~ \$100 – \$225** typical for larger boards from caterers or gourmet shops. citeturn0search2turn0search24turn0search22 | | Extra-Large / Event-sized (15+ guests, grazing tables, or “grazing-table”-style spreads) | **\$200+ – several hundred dollars** — often \$250–\$285 for large pre-made boards, and \$350+ if heavily customized or meant as a main food spread. citeturn0search2turn0search19turn0search24 | ## ⚠️ Why Prices Vary - **Ingredients Quality & Variety**: Cheeses, cured meats, imported or artisanal items — these add up. Premium ingredients push the board toward the higher end of the range. citeturn0search19turn0search6turn0search24 - **Board Type — DIY vs. Pre-Made vs. Catered**: A DIY board (you assemble at home) will often cost less since you're only buying food. Pre-made or catered boards include labor, presentation, and sometimes delivery — thus more expensive. citeturn0search19turn0search24turn0search6 - **Serving Purpose — Appetizer vs. Meal Replacement**: Boards meant just for snacking or appetizers tend to be cheaper. If you expect the board to serve as a full meal, you might order a larger size or more food, which increases cost. citeturn0search2turn0search19turn0search6 - **Customization, Setup, Delivery, Packaging**: Elegant presentation, custom themes (seasonal, holiday, dietary), and delivery or catering add-ons will increase the price. ## 🎉 What You Can Expect in Practice - If you’re hosting a small get-together (around 4–6 people) and want a simple but satisfying charcuterie spread — expect somewhere around **\$50–\$100**. - For a medium-sized party (maybe 8–12 people) with decent variety (meats, cheeses, fruits, crackers) — budget **\$100–\$200**. - For a larger gathering, holiday party, or event where the board may serve as a main food element — plan for **\$200–\$300+**, depending on how lavish you go. --- If you like — I can **pull up 5 full current charcuterie-board pricing examples** (small, medium, large, extra-large) from different vendors right now — might help you see regional/real-world variation (useful in Nashville/US context).
